text: Hi, I'm Vrajesh.
This is Early Bird, my final project.
I am building a tool that makes sure I never miss a new software or A I role.
Here is what it does, and why it matters.
Early Bird will watch the career pages of the twenty-five to thirty companies I choose,
and tell me only about postings that are new.
I want to apply to every software and A I role, so the problem is not too many jobs.
The problem is missing one.
A posting can go up, and I only find out days later.
Early Bird will make sure I hear about each new role the next time I run it,
with referrals first, then freshness, then how well it matches my own projects.
The roles on screen are sample data.
So what already exists?
Here are three kinds of tools.
Job alert emails, which I expect to be broad and often late.
Job trackers, which I expect to record where I applied, but not find new postings.
And scripts that watch one kind of job board. I ran one of these, greenhouse watch, on my Commure snapshots.
It kept a marketing job, because the posting mentioned Python and S Q L.
That is the gap Early Bird will close, by reading each posting with Claude.
Early Bird will use my list, show only what is new, and put referrals first.
Here is how I will build it.
First, fetch. Early Bird will read the public job boards of Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby.
These are public data, with no login. In my Commure test, one snapshot had eighty one postings.
Second, compare. Early Bird will check each posting against a file of what I have already seen. In my test, twelve of the eighty one were new.
Third, judge. Plain rules will come first. Then Claude Sonnet five point five will read each posting.
It will never skip a job for a skill gap. It will only flag a hard blocker, and quote the line.
My probe showed why. A rule alone matched a sales job called Account Executive, A I Sales.
Fourth, match. Each posting will be matched to my real GitHub projects.
Fifth, order. Referral first, then freshness, then match.
For referrals, Early Bird will look up my own LinkedIn connections file, and that file will stay on my laptop.
Sixth, a report, one file for each run.
Do I have what I need? Yes.
Claude access is set up.
The job board data is public, so no account is needed.
I have my own LinkedIn connections export.
And it all runs on my laptop, by hand.
And here is how I will know it works.
Four checks, set before I run anything.
Nothing repeated. Run it twice, and no old posting should come back. My Commure test already did this: eighty postings, then eighty one, with twelve new.
Nothing missed. At least ninety five percent of the roles I mark as relevant.
Honest blockers. Every flag must quote the line from the posting.
Right contact. The referral match must agree with my own check.
I will lock my labels before the first run.
It worked if all four checks pass.
If any check fails, I will report the miss and say what broke.
One known risk. On one posting, three Claude runs read two plus years as not entry level. My own rule keeps anything under three years.
That is Early Bird.
Thank you. This was read by a synthetic voice, from a script drafted with Claude from my decisions.
